title: Back off fingerprint retries that fail immediately
head: c6e44e9fa76a
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A single PamContext error consumes two backoff slots, reaching 30 seconds after four errors
leads.consequence: Quickshell emits error then completed(Error) for one failure. Both handlers call scheduleFingerprintRetry, which increments the count twice and restarts the timer twice. In a synthetic signal-order replay, the first device error waits 500ms rather than the intended 250ms and the second waits 2000ms rather than 500ms; four errors reach the 30s cap. A user returning to a briefly unavailable reader may wait longer for fingerprint recovery; password still works. Schedule in one handler or deduplicate per attempt, and assert signal-pair behavior.

leads.summary: A no-finger timeout is classified as a mismatch and clears the backoff even though the reader was armed
leads.consequence: When no finger is presented, pam_fprintd waits up to its default 30s then returns PAM_AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL. This takes the >=1s branch and resets the error streak, although there was no successful scan or user interaction. A thermally limited device can be heated by prolonged armed verify sessions with only 250ms idle between them until it starts rejecting attempts; after cooling enough to accept a session the idle wait again clears the streak. The PR's statement that a long attempt is an ordinary mismatch is false for this real dependency output. Distinguish a true scan/prompt/timeout from elapsed time, and consider idling the reader when the display is blank, as the overlapping #11273/#12420 proposals do. Hardware-dependent thermal effect is not live-tested.
leads.triage: overlaps Opus F2: the 30 s no-finger timeout resets the streak and back-to-back armed verifies reheat; folded into thermal finding, not a separate defect (reset on timeout is intended)

leads.summary: The new test can pass when the production classifier is disabled
leads.consequence: The test declares local JavaScript constants instead of reading the actual QML properties. A disposable head copy with fingerprintImmediateFailureMs changed from 1000 to 0 has no immediate-failure classification for nonnegative elapsed time, but all 16 test assertions pass because the test still supplies 1000. Read constants from the QML source or add a realistic QML/component-level test, and include error plus completed in the same test.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus test-gap note; Opus run3 confirmed fingerprintImmediateFailureMs 0 passes all 16

They are diverged and each is MERGEABLE against the base, but the three-way Service.qml merge has two conflict blocks in failure scheduling and onError, with two fingerprintRetryBaseMs declarations even outside conflict blocks. Choosing both naively would leave duplicate declarations and opposed scheduling logic. Explicitly select one policy, reconcile the error-plus-completed signal pair, and rerun whichever tests remain.

leads.summary: A fingerprint status probe can rearm a pending backed-off retry early
leads.consequence: Once an immediate failure starts a long retry timer, a concurrently completing availability probe that still reports yes invokes startFingerprint directly while the timer is running, with no check or cancellation. beginLock queues the probe and IPC preview also invokes it, so a late initial probe or preview call during a lock can launch a new PAM session ahead of a thermal cooldown. This is one premature attempt per probe, not proof of a sustained storm; no live timing was tested. Avoid starting a new attempt while a retry is pending unless intentionally overriding the delay on explicit user input.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up (opus/followup-direct-start.md) confirms mechanism but at most one extra attempt per lock via unlikely race or per external preview call with no in-repo caller; not material

The fprintd and libfprint source clones are unpinned upstream tips, not a proven Arch package build. Thermal consequence is conditional on a thermally guarded reader. Headless synthetic tests establish JavaScript state, not full QML rendering or Qt signal delivery.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Each immediate fingerprint PAM error advances the backoff twice, so retries wait 500, 2000, 8000, then 30000 ms instead of 250, 500, 1000, 2000 ms.

### A PAM error counts twice

Quickshell's `PamContext` emits `error()` then `completed(PamResult.Error)` for one attempt, and both `fingerprintPam.onError` and `handleFingerprintFinished` call `scheduleFingerprintRetry()`. The named failures (hot, unplugged or claimed reader, fprintd gone) reach QML as `error()`, since pam_fprintd returns `PAM_AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL`. **Impact:** the 30 s ceiling arrives at the 4th immediate error, not the 8th; the test calls the scheduler once per failure, so it misses this.

**Suggested change:** keep only `root.fingerprintAuthenticating = false` in `onError`, and replace the test's second assertion with a replay of `onError` then `onCompleted`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at c6e44e9)</summary>

# Reproducer: a fingerprint PAM error is counted twice by the backoff

Reviewed head: `c6e44e9fa76a976661e38f2cbab74e8d3228ea93` (omacom/omarchy PR #11918). The same result was obtained with the PR merged onto `quattro` at `8b4eae66`.

**What it shows.** Quickshell's `PamContext::onError` emits `error()` and then `completed(PamResult::Error)` for the same conversation (quickshell v0.3.1 `src/services/pam/qml.cpp`, lines 203-207, unchanged since v0.2.0). pam_fprintd returns `PAM_AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL` for a reader that is too hot (fprintd maps `FP_DEVICE_ERROR_TOO_HOT` to `verify-disconnected`), unplugged, claimed elsewhere, or when fprintd is unreachable, and Quickshell reports that code through `error()`. At the reviewed head both the `onError` handler and `handleFingerprintFinished` call `scheduleFingerprintRetry()`, so one immediate failure increments `fingerprintImmediateFailures` twice.

This is a Node replay in the style of `test/shell.d/lock-fingerprint-retry-test.sh`: it extracts the real `fingerprintRetryDelay`, `scheduleFingerprintRetry`, `handleFingerprintFinished` and the `fingerprintPam` `onError`/`onCompleted` bodies from `Service.qml` and calls the two handlers in Quickshell's order. It does not run Quickshell or PAM.

**Run.** Save the file below as `test/shell.d/lock-fingerprint-pam-error-test.sh` in a checkout of the PR head and run `bash test/shell.d/lock-fingerprint-pam-error-test.sh` (needs Node).

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

run_node_test <<'JS'
const fs = require('fs')
const lockSource = fs.readFileSync(root + '/shell/plugins/lock/Service.qml', 'utf8')

const grab = (pattern, description) => {
  const match = lockSource.match(pattern)
  assert(match, description)
  return match
}

// Stand-ins for the QML root. The handler bodies below use `root.x`, so a
// proxy maps those names onto these bindings.
const PamResult = { Success: 0, Failed: 1, Error: 2, MaxTries: 3 }
const PamError = { StartFailed: 1, TryAuthFailed: 2, InternalError: 3 }
var lockRequested = true
var fingerprintConfigured = true
var fingerprintAuthenticating = false
var fingerprintImmediateFailures = 0
var fingerprintStartedAt = 0
var fingerprintRetryBaseMs = 250
var fingerprintRetryMaxMs = 30000
var fingerprintImmediateFailureMs = 1000
var fingerprintRetryTimer = { interval: 0, restart() {} }
function finishUnlock() {}

eval(grab(/  function fingerprintRetryDelay\([\s\S]*?\n  \}/, 'the retry delay curve is present')[0])
eval(grab(/  function scheduleFingerprintRetry\([\s\S]*?\n  \}/, 'the retry scheduler is present')[0])
eval(grab(/  function handleFingerprintFinished\([\s\S]*?\n  \}/, 'the completion handler is present')[0])

const pamBlock = grab(/id: fingerprintPam\b[\s\S]*?\n  \}/, 'the fingerprint PamContext is present')[0]
const onErrorBody = pamBlock.match(/onError: function\(error\) \{([\s\S]*?)\n    \}/)
const onCompletedBody = pamBlock.match(/onCompleted: function\(result\) \{([\s\S]*?)\n    \}/)
assert(onErrorBody && onCompletedBody, 'the fingerprint PamContext handles error and completed')

const qmlRoot = new Proxy({}, {
  get: (_, name) => eval(name),
  set: (_, name, value) => { eval(name + ' = value'); return true },
})
const onError = new Function('root', 'error', onErrorBody[1])
const onCompleted = new Function('root', 'result', onCompletedBody[1])

// Quickshell's PamContext::onError (src/services/pam/qml.cpp) emits error()
// and then completed(PamResult::Error) for the same conversation. pam_fprintd
// returns PAM_AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL for a reader that is too hot, unplugged or
// claimed elsewhere, and Quickshell reports that code through error(), so a
// single failed attempt runs both handlers.
function pamErrorAfter(elapsedMs) {
  fingerprintStartedAt = Date.now() - elapsedMs
  onError(qmlRoot, PamError.TryAuthFailed)
  onCompleted(qmlRoot, PamResult.Error)
  return fingerprintRetryTimer.interval
}

const intervals = []
for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) intervals.push(pamErrorAfter(0))
console.log(`# retry intervals after 5 immediate PAM errors: ${intervals.join(', ')} ms`)
console.log(`# fingerprintImmediateFailures after 5 immediate PAM errors: ${fingerprintImmediateFailures}`)

assertEqual(intervals[0], 250, 'the first immediate PAM error retries at the base interval')
assertEqual(fingerprintImmediateFailures, 5, 'each failed attempt counts once toward the backoff')
assertEqual(intervals.join(','), '250,500,1000,2000,4000', 'immediate PAM errors follow the documented curve')

// A PAM error after pam_fprintd's 30 s no-finger timeout is not a reader fault.
assertEqual(pamErrorAfter(30000), 250, 'a timed-out attempt retries promptly')
assertEqual(fingerprintImmediateFailures, 0, 'a timed-out attempt clears the backoff')
JS
```

**Actual output at the reviewed head** (exit status 1):

```
ok - the retry delay curve is present
ok - the retry scheduler is present
ok - the completion handler is present
ok - the fingerprint PamContext is present
ok - the fingerprint PamContext handles error and completed
# retry intervals after 5 immediate PAM errors: 500, 2000, 8000, 30000, 30000 ms
# fingerprintImmediateFailures after 5 immediate PAM errors: 10
expected: 250
actual:   500
not ok - the first immediate PAM error retries at the base interval
```

**With the `onError` handler reduced to clearing `fingerprintAuthenticating`** (so only `completed(PamResult.Error)` schedules the retry), the same test passes (exit status 0):

```diff
     onError: function(error) {
       root.fingerprintAuthenticating = false
-      if (root.lockRequested && root.fingerprintConfigured) root.scheduleFingerprintRetry()
     }
```

```
ok - the retry delay curve is present
ok - the retry scheduler is present
ok - the completion handler is present
ok - the fingerprint PamContext is present
ok - the fingerprint PamContext handles error and completed
# retry intervals after 5 immediate PAM errors: 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000 ms
# fingerprintImmediateFailures after 5 immediate PAM errors: 5
ok - the first immediate PAM error retries at the base interval
ok - each failed attempt counts once toward the backoff
ok - immediate PAM errors follow the documented curve
ok - a timed-out attempt retries promptly
ok - a timed-out attempt clears the backoff
```

With that change, the PR's own `lock-fingerprint-retry-test.sh` fails its second assertion, because that assertion requires the `onError` call (exit status 1):

```
ok - a failed fingerprint match is rescheduled through the backoff
not ok - a fingerprint PAM error is rescheduled through the backoff
```
</details>

<details><summary>More findings: the thermal comment claims more than the backoff does</summary>

libfprint refuses a verify on a hot reader and returns `FP_DEVICE_ERROR_TOO_HOT` without counting the attempt as active time (`fp-device.c`, `fp_device_verify()`). A hot reader then cools for about 205 s whatever the retry rate, and the back-to-back 30 s armed verifies (pam_fprintd's default no-finger timeout) are what heat it again. **Impact:** the Service.qml comment ("a reader waiting to cool never gets the idle time it needs to recover") and the commit message present the backoff as the fix for thermal lockouts, but it reduces the churn, not the lockout.

**Suggested change:** reword the comment and commit message to claim only the reduction in PAM sessions while the reader cannot work.

Synthetic model only (libfprint's temperature logic re-implemented from source with default constants, one unattended hour, 50 ms of overhead per attempt assumed); not run on hardware. Drivers that opt out of the model were not examined.

| policy | PAM sessions | each hot phase | reader unusable (hot, or cooled but not yet re-armed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| merge-base (flat 250 ms) | 7,572 | 205.5 s | 62.7% |
| this PR as written | 151 | 221 s | 61.1% |
| this PR, one count per attempt | 188 | 213 s | 58.8% |
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified**
- The PR's test passes at c6e44e9 and with the PR merged onto `quattro` 8b4eae66, and fails against the merge-base `Service.qml`.
- `fingerprintRetryDelay()` gives 250 ms for 0 or 1 failures, then doubles, capped at 30 s.
- `resetAuthenticationState()` clears the streak on lock and unlock; an aborted attempt never reaches `scheduleFingerprintRetry()`.
- With pam_fprintd's defaults (3 tries, 30 s timeout), a wrong finger or no finger ends an attempt well after 1 s, so the 1 s cut-off separates those from immediate device failures.
- Full `./test/shell`: the same 6 files fail at the merge-base and at c6e44e9, and the same 15 at the `quattro` tip with and without the PR, so none is caused by this change.

**Optional notes**
- The test declares its own `250/30000/1000` constants, so changing the QML properties (for example `fingerprintImmediateFailureMs` to 0) still passes all 16 assertions; reading the values from `Service.qml` would catch that.
- Once backed off, a user who returns after the fault clears can wait up to 30 s before a touch works (password entry is unaffected); restarting a backed-off timer at the base interval on a key press or click would avoid that.

**Related open PRs**
- #10393, #7158 and #12291 each add `test/shell.d/lock-fingerprint-retry-test.sh`, so at most one can keep that name.
- #12291 adds `property int fingerprintRetryDelay` and its own `scheduleFingerprintRetry()`, clashing with this PR's function names; #12544 also declares `fingerprintRetryBaseMs`.
- #7179, #10393, #10653, #11273, #12461, #12544, #7158, #8531, #11162 and #12291 conflict textually with this PR in `Service.qml`. #10393, #12461 and #7179 already avoid the double count; #10653 and #11273 schedule from both handlers too.
</details>
